title: Combining metabolome and clinical indicators with machine learning provides some promising diagnostic markers to precisely detect smear-positive/negative pulmonary tuberculosis
summary: The study reports altered fatty-acid and amino-acid metabolite patterns and candidate marker combinations for three TB/control groups; this is a small retrospective biomarker result, not established clinical utility. Primary Methods/Results report 27 smear-positive cases, 37 smear-negative cases and 36 controls; RF performance is checked with SVM and MLP on the same study cohort. Independent external validation is not reported.
ai_technology: Random forest selects metabolite/clinical feature combinations from plasma metabolomics for smear-positive, smear-negative and control classification.
